title: Open files
line: Rooks belong where the pawns have gone.

steps.text: A rook needs open lines. Behind its own pawns it does little. Each side here has lost the same pawn in the center.
A file with no pawns on it at all is an open file. Tap any square on the open file.
steps.hint: Look for the one column from your side to Black's with no pawn of either color.
steps.after: Nothing blocks a rook there, from one end of the board to the other.

steps.text: Black's rooks cannot reach that file yet. Put your rook from the corner on it.

also.f1d1: That rook works too. This lesson moves the one doing nothing in the corner.
also.f3e5: That knight move is as strong. This lesson is about the rook.

wrong.a2a4: That leaves the open file to Black.

steps.after: Your rook owns the open file. Black's knight steps aside.

steps.text: Use the file: send the rook deep into Black's side, to a square no black pawn can attack.

also.f3e5: That is as strong. This lesson goes on with the rook.

steps.after: Black brings its rook to the middle. Your rook sits deep in Black's half, where no black pawn can attack it.

summary: An open file has no pawns. Put your rooks there first, then use it to get into the other side.
